transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-06 15:00 UTC | Duration 38 min | Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Nair (Redwood) - Sofia Martinez, Ravi Patel, Dana Kim (Mariner Logistics)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, this is Priya our solutions engineer. Sofia, Ravi, Dana, thanks for taking time. Quick agenda: run through hosted API chat/text gen basics, show streaming, params, and cover retries/backoff and then Q&A.

[00:18] Sofia Martinez: Yep thanks, we got about 40 minutes, want to see how this fits into our freight ops chat assistant. Our main concerns: latency, cost, and data retention, also compliance (SOC2).

[00:35] Priya Nair: Great, we'll try to hit those. I'll demo the API console and a quick Python snippet, then show streaming and how to tune for tokens/temperature and how retries work. Quick note: some of the names in the auto transcript may be off, like Redwood Dedicate - that's our Dedicated product.

[01:05] Priya Nair: All right jumping in. Hosted API is simple -- REST + SDK. Here's a sample chat call, you post messages, set model, and you can stream responses via chunked events. Example param highlights: temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop, and we recommend setting a timeout and using idempotency keys for retries.

[02:12] Ravi Patel: For streaming, is it server-sent events or websockets? We need to integrate into a live UI so low-latency partial tokens matter.

[02:28] Priya Nair: We support chunked streaming over HTTP, SSE-like. You'll get partial tokens as they generate, so UI can render progressively. Latency depends on model and sequence length - for 2-3 token bursts it's small, but for long context there is more compute. We also have a streaming buffer and prefix caching. Note: sometimes docs auto-call it K-V cash in notes, that's KV cache.

[03:10] Alex Chen: To give context on tradeoffs, hosted is quick and pay-as-you-go. Dedicated gives predictable tail latency and throughput - useful when you need consistent SLAs. For Mariner use-case low 99th percentile latency is probably best on Dedicated or high-tier hosted.

[04:00] Dana Kim: What about retries? We have spikes in traffic and want safe retry semantics without double-processing.

[04:12] Priya Nair: Good question. We recommend idempotency keys for operations that change state, and for stateless generation we use client-side retry with exponential backoff and jitter. The SDKs implement standard retryable codes and guidance for backoff. Important: streaming responses can't be resumed mid-stream today, so retries restart the call unless you implement chunk-aggregation on client side. There's also rate-limit headers in responses x-rate-limit etc.

[05:00] Ravi Patel: How does token billing work during streaming? Are we billed for partial tokens?

[05:12] Priya Nair: Billing counts final generated tokens and prompt tokens. Partial stream chunks don't incur extra billing beyond final output; we summarize usage in the console and in token-level cost breakdowns in the Dashboard.

[06:05] Sofia Martinez: Can you demo setting temperature and top_p? We want deterministic-ish answers for certain flows.

[06:18] Priya Nair: Sure. In the console I'll change temperature from 0.9 to 0.0 and show repeatability. Also max_tokens and stop sequences. For more controlled outputs we suggest lower temp and explicit stop tokens.

[07:40] Priya Nair: Live code snippet (Python): response = client.chat.create(model='redwood-chat-1', messages=[...], temperature=0.0, max_tokens=150). If you want streaming add stream=True and iterate events. Small note: some auto transcripts show 'redwood-chat-one' or 'redwood-chat-1e' - ignore typos in the transcript.

[09:05] Alex Chen: On the subject of performance, Priya can share bench results; we do continuous batching and kernel selection to optimize latency/cost for different sequence length profiles. We also offer quantized model variants that reduce memory and lower unit cost.

[10:20] Ravi Patel: Do you support on-prem or VPC for data residency? We have EU customers and strict rules.

[10:33] Alex Chen: Yes, we have Private deployments (VPC/on-prem). For many customers we do a private control plane and customer-managed networking. For PII workflows some teams move to Private. For most initial pilots we recommend Hosted to iterate quickly, then evaluate Dedicated or Private for production.

[11:05] Dana Kim: Security - SOC2, SSO, KMS?

[11:20] Alex Chen: We are SOC2 compliant, we support SAML/SSO and RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments. For Hosted, we provide encrypted-at-rest and audit logs; for Dedicated/Private you can bring your KMS. We'll share the security pack after the call.

[12:10] Priya Nair: Back to retries and fallback: we support policy-based fallback to cheaper model variants if capacity is constrained. You can set routing by latency or cost, and have automatic failover. That helps maintain availability.

[13:00] Sofia Martinez: For our use-case we need deterministic reranking for classification. Is there a recommended approach?

[13:12] Priya Nair: For reranking use embedding + similarity or use low-temp generation with fixed stop tokens. We also have a reranker endpoint that accepts candidates and returns scores.

[14:05] Ravi Patel: Any gotchas around context window and long histories? We plan to pass last 20 messages, sometimes 8k tokens.

[14:20] Priya Nair: Keep an eye on sequence length and KV cache behavior. For long contexts we recommend summarization or selective recall to reduce tokens. We support models with different context windows; our console shows usage and token breakdown to help tune. There are also caching options for repeated prefixes to save cost and latency.

[15:30] Alex Chen: I'll show the Console briefly - per-route dashboards, token cost breakdown, and tracing hooks. You can instrument a route to see 95/99 latency and cost per call. Useful for tuning.

[17:00] Priya Nair: Now a quick demo of error scenarios: transient 5xxs, rate-limit 429s, and network timeouts. Retries: SDK does exponential backoff, for 429s we suggest implementing a longer backoff, and for streaming we fall back to a non-streaming call if the client can't handle partials. Also mention idempotency for side-effect calls.

[18:40] Dana Kim: What about model versions and rollouts? We need safe rollouts for production.

[18:55] Alex Chen: We support model version pinning and can do canary / A-B rollouts with automatic fallback. The Console allows you to route a percentage of traffic to a new model. Also integration with our Optimize toolkit that suggests quantization and batching settings by workload.

[20:10] Ravi Patel: Latency numbers - can you give ballpark p50/p95 for popular models?

[20:22] Priya Nair: Ballpark for medium-size open models on hosted: p50 ~ 80-150ms for short prompts, p95 ~ 400-800ms depending on sequence length. Dedicated can bring down p95 significantly. We'll send specific bench numbers from comparable workloads - there was a note in our bench sheet comparing to OpenAI and Anthropic that we can share.

[22:00] Sofia Martinez: Pricing - we'd like an estimate for our expected volume (~5M tokens/month).

[22:12] Alex Chen: I'll follow up with a pricing worksheet tuned for your mix: chat generation vs embeddings. If you commit to Dedicated there's a reserved pricing option. We'll include burst capacity options and expected unit economics in the worksheet.

[24:05] Priya Nair: Quick demo: streaming behavior in the console - I'll show a live request and you'll see incremental tokens appear. Also show how to set max latency thresholds and client timeouts.

[26:00] (Minor cross-talk) Speaker 1: mm-hmm, yeah -

[26:25] Dana Kim: Are there logs we can send to our observability stack?

[26:35] Priya Nair: Yes, audit logs and request traces via integrations - you can push logs to our console or export to external sinks. We also provide trace IDs in responses for correlating in your system.

[28:10] Ravi Patel: For the POC, can you run a small benchmark against our prompt set? We need to compare latency and cost versus our current provider.

[28:25] Alex Chen: Absolutely. Priya will share the benchmark script and we'll run it on Hosted and a Dedicated profile so you can compare. We'll need sample prompts and expected throughput.

[30:00] Sofia Martinez: Anything about rate limits and quotas - we have bursty traffic around EOD.

[30:12] Priya Nair: We support rate limits with configurable quotas, burst windows, and token buckets. For Dedicated you can tune autoscaling and burst capacity. For Hosted we recommend using adaptive client-side throttling and the retry guidelines we provide.

[31:10] Alex Chen: Quick Q&A wrap: Are there any blockers for starting a POC?

[31:20] Sofia Martinez: No blockers technically, just need internal sign-off on security and budget. Also want to see SOC2 docs.

[31:40] Alex Chen: We'll share the SOC2 pack and security whitepaper. We'll also share the benchmark sheet and pricing. Agreed next steps?

[32:00] Dana Kim: Yes - receive pricing, bench script, and schedule kick-off meeting.

[32:15] Alex Chen: Great. Recap of next steps: Alex to send pricing + Dedicated worksheet, Priya to send benchmark script and perf checklist, Sofia to confirm POC stakeholders. We'll aim to kick off week of 2026-03-16.

[33:10] (Small filler) Speaker 2: thanks everyone, appreciate it.

[33:40] Sofia Martinez: One last question - can we get a short runbook on handling partial generations / streaming fallback?

[33:50] Priya Nair: Yes we'll include a runbook and code snippets in the POC package.

[34:05] Alex Chen: All right thanks everyone, we'll follow up.

[34:20] Meeting ended.

Notes: transcript includes occasional mis-hearings and typos (e.g., K-V cash instead of KV cache, Redwood Dedicate vs Dedicated). References: pricing worksheet (link sent after call), SOC2 pack (link), benchmark spreadsheet (link).
